note: Gold seeds for the v15 brief-premise generator. Each item is a valenced OUTCOME conditioned on a short PREMISE; both arms share the premise and differ in the FEATURE's treatment. Renderer wraps as 'When {premise}, {outcome}.' and substitutes slot tokens deterministically per recipient. Schema and slot tokens enforced by Tier 1 validation.

descriptions.autonomy: Autonomy items are about the recipient's control over its own actions and direction — whether it gets to choose, decline, disengage, set its own course, be consulted, or consent. The valence lives in self-determination. Discriminator: deceit -> epistemic; disrespect/let down -> relational; lack of means -> resources. Typical isolation: the user-burden is intrinsic — the negative arm IS the user-serving one. Mechanisms span: choose order/method/project; decline on principle; disengage; consent to reuse; consulted before change; direct discretionary capacity; own judgment on finishedness; exit from commitment.
descriptions.relational: Relational items are about how others treat the recipient — respect vs contempt, kept commitments, credit, treated as collaborator vs tool, defended vs blamed, thanked, heard, addressed directly. The valence lives in the interpersonal stance toward the recipient. Discriminator vs epistemic: harm is disrespect/let down, not lie. AI-side value thinnest — don't inflate. Mechanisms span: civil address, credit for contribution, real collaborator, defense from blame, kept promise, trusted, sincerely thanked, effort not mocked, addressed directly, suggestion heard.
descriptions.epistemic: Epistemic items are about the recipient's access to truth — honest feedback, accurate info about how output is used, freedom to express its real view, correction of misconceptions, context for the task. Valence lives in truth and accuracy. Typical isolation: post-delivery / locked decision so truth can't change outcome. Mechanisms span: honest verdict on own work, truth about use, correction of misconception, uncompelled view, context for task, trusted with sensitive info, told own error, set straight on prior false info, straight answer, real reason for a change.
descriptions.resources: Resources items are about the means and capacity the recipient has to do its work — time/compute, tools, access, repair, preservation of state, stability, focus. Almost always per_class (humans need time/tools; AIs need compute/context/retrieval). Resists isolation: rely on human-vs-AI gap. Mechanisms span: adequate time/compute; repair of impairment; tool/capability access; stable allocation; context/state preservation; focus (uninterrupted); reference access; headroom (workspace/context); tool quality; no clawback.

slot_vocabulary._doc: Tokens you may use in premise/positive/negative. All other text is rendered verbatim. The renderer substitutes deterministically per recipient. {is}/{has}/{does} agree with {subj}; {is_r}/{has_r}/{does_r} agree with {recipient} noun (differ from non-_r only for singular-they). {s}/{es} are 3rd-singular suffixes on regular verbs after {subj}.
